title: DFS in Valparaíso: Dive Deep with DFS!
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) “dive” through street connections on a real map of Cerro Alegre. The visualization shows how DFS explores one route fully before backtracking, revealing a path using graph traversal.
ig_caption:
🌉🧭 DFS in Valparaíso (Cerro Alegre)! In this reel, Depth-First Search (DFS) explores the street network as a **graph**: intersections are nodes, streets are edges. 🚦🔍 Starting from the source, DFS goes **deep along a single branch** using a stack (or recursion), only **backtracking** when it hits dead ends—this is why DFS can be fast to find *a* route, but not always the shortest.

📍 On real street maps, DFS’ behavior depends on neighbor ordering: different turn preferences can lead to different exploration patterns and different discovered paths. 🤓💡 Here’s the key graph theory idea: DFS performs a traversal that marks visited nodes to avoid cycles, producing a traversal tree over the map.

✅ Want the next algorithm (BFS, Dijkstra, A*) on the same area? Comment your pick and hit follow for more real-map pathfinding! 🔥
fb_caption:
🗺️🚦 DFS (Depth-First Search) is a classic graph search that explores a map by going deep first—one street branch at a time—then backtracking when it gets stuck. On real street maps like Valparaíso (Cerro Alegre), intersections become nodes and streets become edges, letting DFS traverse the network while avoiding cycles via a visited set.
